schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The == compare, living in exactly one place. A gate holds a PROOF RECORD — one entry per check that ran, each stating what was EXPECTED beside what was ACTUAL — and it OPENS when every entry's expected equals its actual. `verdict(record)` returns OPEN/CLOSED, the count of checks, THE LIST OF WHAT IT PROVED BY NAME, and the mismatches whole. `proved(...)` builds an entry so every gate in the system emits the same shape, and `passed(entry)` is the entire decision procedure. NO EMPTY ANYWHERE: an empty record RAISES `NoProof` (`all([])` is True, which is how the vacuous green ships without anyone noticing), and an entry missing `expected` or `actual` raises rather than being skipped, because a skipped entry means the gate opened on fewer checks than it claims. Values compare as canonical JSON so key order cannot decide a verdict, and an unserializable value renders rather than raising — a gate that crashes on an odd value fails open inside any caller that wraps it. IT HOLDS NO STATE; the record arrives as an argument and nothing is remembered between calls. It contains no branch that could consult anything: the primitive that makes 'no gate consults an oracle' enforceable cannot itself be the exception.
why: Akien, 2026-08-13, in three rulings that are one ruling: 'NO GATES MAY CONSULT ORACLES EVER PERIOD. A GATE ONLY OPENS WHEN A FINDINGS REPORT MATCHES WHAT IT ALLOWS. ITS AN == compare. Must be identical. NO ORACLE.' — then, on this module's first cut: 'The build inspector must list EVERY TEST THAT HAS PASSED. {EXPECTED: value, ACTUAL: value} ... NO EMPTY ANYWHERE.' — then the general form: 'EVERYTHING ALWAYS PROVED AND LISTING WHAT IT PROVED. SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE.' THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is why a findings report cannot be what a gate reads: a findings list holds only what went WRONG, so an empty one means 'every check passed' AND 'no check ran' AND 'the census found no components' AND 'the walk crashed early', and nothing downstream can tell those apart. A gate over that has a green about SILENCE. build_inspector had exactly this: `clean: not findings`, and its own charter records the day the whole sweep read a directory that no longer existed and came back clean — 'vacuously green is the worst colour a gate can be.' A proof record cannot be silent, because it names every check that ran; a sieve that stops running makes the list SHORTER rather than CLEANER, and short is readable. SECOND SYMPTOM, the one that made gate-ness worth berthing at all: it lived in PROSE. build_inspector's charter said it was a gate and said gates are inference-free; `cairn determinism` could report where the LLM was but could not red a gate for reaching one, because nothing on disk said which components WERE gates. A rule you have to remember to apply is not enforced (Law 4). One importable module turns gate-ness into an IMPORT FACT the same walk already reads.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.gate import gate` — `gate.proved(identity=, expected=, actual=, location=, code=, source=, **values)` to build an entry, `gate.verdict(record)` for the full answer, `gate.opens(record)` for the boolean. No CLI door: a gate is composed by the component doing the gating, never run at a person. `cairn determinism` reports which components reach it and reds any that also reach an oracle. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/gate/proofs/test_gate.py`.
entry: FRESH build, 2026-08-13. Nothing was grafted, and one thing was deliberately COMPOSED rather than re-derived: the record shape is `SEED` from cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector — identity, location, code, expected, actual, fatality, source, plus the every-value-that-bears-on-the-fault clause — which is Akien's own list, settled in 2007 and already in this corpus. This module names that vocabulary and does NOT re-implement completeness checking over it; measuring whether a record honours its seed is diagnostic_inspector's job and it already does it. The compare it replaces was also already here, written longhand as `clean: not findings` inside build_inspector, where nothing could see it was a gate.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, BORN AT THIS ADDRESS'S FIRST CROSSING. Until a ticket crosses here there is no journal, and that absence is this component's ordinary resting state rather than a missing file — a component that has never sailed has no voyage to record. CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (ticket a-charter-may-not-assert-a-file-that-is-not-there).
how_it_learns: IT DOESN'T, AND THAT IS THE POINT — this is the one component where learning would be the defect. A gate that adjusts its own compare is a gate that opens on something other than ==, which is what Akien forbade. What learns is the INSPECTOR that produces the record: the questions get better, the record gets more entries, and Akien expects exactly that ('We might have to add more or better inspection questions, but that's fine. we learn as we go'). An inspector may hold a SLEEP seam and be MOSTLY DETERMINISTIC; the gate must be PURE. That split is the architecture, and this module is the half that does not move. The record shape is how the learning stays legible: a new question shows up as a new named entry with its own expected and actual, not as a change to what passing means.
filed_edges: (a) NOTHING RECORDS WHO SET AN EXPECTATION. Every entry today expects 1.0 because build_inspector's sieves score 0/1, so the expectation is structural and nobody had to choose it. The moment a gate expects a value somebody DECIDED, the record needs to carry who decided it and when — an expectation without that is a green somebody granted and nobody signed.

(b) THE RECORD IS BUILT, NOT PERSISTED. `verdict` is computed per run and thrown away. Nothing compares this run's record to the last one, so a check that silently STOPS RUNNING shortens the list and nobody is told — the very failure this shape exists to make visible is currently visible only to a human reading two runs side by side. This is the next real build.

(c) SEED COMPLETENESS IS NOT ENFORCED HERE, BY DESIGN, AND THEREFORE NOT ENFORCED ANYWHERE ON THIS PATH. `proved()` fills the seed shape, but a caller who builds an entry by hand needs only identity/expected/actual to get a verdict. diagnostic_inspector measures completeness and is not wired to build_inspector's record.
(d) NO CLI DOOR, DELIBERATELY. There is nothing a person would run this at. If a view is ever wanted it is `cairn determinism` growing a `--gates` surface, not a second door here.

(e) SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE IS RULED, NOT YET DONE. Akien ruled the pattern for the whole system; one component emits it. The derivation gate, the ruling intake, the emit chokepoint, the tester and `cairn determinism` itself all still report only their failures. Each is its own crossing.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_gate.py (11 teeth, aimed at the ways a proof record decays back into silence, not at equality itself). Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) an EMPTY record produces a verdict instead of raising; (2) a record carrying only failures is indistinguishable from one where every check passed — the passes must be counted and named; (3) an entry missing expected or actual is skipped rather than refused; (4) key order in a structured value changes a verdict; (5) an odd value raises instead of closing, because a raising gate fails open inside any caller that wraps it; (6) `fatality` is read from the caller rather than derived, which would let a caller's opinion of severity into the compare; (7) a prior call changes a later verdict, which would make this a machine that needs an owner; (8) the live inspector's record lists no passes. WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: any argument added to `opens` beyond the record. A tolerance, a mode, a severity floor — each is the compare becoming an opinion.
proof: proofs/test_gate.py — eleven teeth. The load-bearing ones are (c) an EMPTY record raises and (d) the record lists what PASSED, not only what failed; between them they pin the record against the silence it decays into. (k) runs the live inspector and asserts by invariant that its record is non-empty and contains passes — a record carrying only failures would satisfy a naive == check and still be the silence this exists to end. Enforcement of the oracle rule lives at determinism's proof (teeth l, l2, m, n, o, p, q), which the corpus runs — including q, which asserts gates EXIST before asserting none consults an oracle.

feedback.why: A gate verdicts the build inspector's sieve output — the record it opens or closes on is a PRODUCT of sieve calibration. When a gate fires (green or red), the observation (which entries passed, which failed, with what parameter values) is feedback about the calibration that produced the record. The build inspector owns the sieves and their seed parameters; this route delivers the gate's structured observation back to the component whose calibration it measures. The LLM inspection probe reads accumulated feedback at this destination and proposes parameter adjustments through TransitionGate.adjust() — the gate TOOL stays pure (the == compare does not learn), but the PARAMETERS that produce the record the gate compares are the inspector's to calibrate, and calibration needs this signal.

owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Akien owns the definition — the == compare, the absolute rule over gates, and the proof-record shape are all his, ruled 2026-08-13. CC writes the code and the proofs.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — this is the physics under 'no gate consults an oracle', replacing the prose IOU)
Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — an empty record IS the hollow build, and it raises)
Law 9 (red is the default; a record that lists every check cannot inherit a green from silence)
Law 7 (a gate's verdict is permanent in a record of truth, so it must replay — which is why a gate may not even have a SLEEP seam)
Law 1 (the compare lives once; build_inspector's longhand `not findings` was the same compare re-derived, and the record shape is diagnostic_inspector's SEED rather than a second vocabulary)

Law 6 (it has USERS and not an owner — because whatever state a tool carries berths under its holder and is the holder's to gate, so the tool has nothing of its own to gate; ruling 2026-08-14-tools-and-machines-remember-under-their-holder, which corrected the earlier wording here that traced Law 6 to statelessness)
provenance: Born 2026-08-13 and rebuilt the same day. The first cut read Akien's 'what it allows' as an EXEMPTION LIST — a findings report compared against allowed findings — which he refused outright: 'why would build inspector declare []. That is ABSOLUTELY WRONG. The build inspector must list EVERY TEST THAT HAS PASSED.' The correction is not a detail: an exemption list is a record of what we tolerate, and a proof record is a record of what we know. He then gave the general form ('SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE') and named the fields, which turned out to be the SEED already sitting in diagnostic_inspector — his own 2007 list, which the first cut walked past. Rebuilt on the record, the live gate reads 720 checks · 697 proved · 23 failed, where the exemption reading had reported '359 findings' and nothing about the 697.
learns: It does not; it is a pure gate function — it opens or closes on an equality compare.
